decision: Bake enumerates the whole Data tree; coverage = parsed/total of files that exist
why: Armed goal is 100% corpus coverage, not a 2–3 map slice. Missing catalog slots are listed, never invented.
revisit: When a real client Data pack is attached, re-run bake and treat ImageDecodePercent as the gate metric.

decision: Client runtime stays .Lib; WIL/WZL/WTL are bake/editor inputs
why: Matches Client/MirGraphics/MLibrary.cs. Inventing a second runtime loader would fork protocol-adjacent content.
revisit: If a private server still ships raw WIL only, bake must convert before Client.Linux can draw.

decision: IRenderer + SlimDX adapter instead of deleting D3D9 this PR
why: Smallest lever: MLibrary draws move off Sprite.Draw while GameScene RTs still compile.
revisit: Next: RTs, CMain present loop, Line/Label locks.

decision: Silk.NET.OpenGL for the Linux backend
why: Pure .NET, Linux-viable, no native project. Windowing is optional; NullRenderer covers headless CI.
revisit: Vulkan/wgpu only if OpenGL drivers become the blocker.

decision: Client.Linux is the Linux compile target; Client.csproj stays net8.0-windows
why: WinForms + SlimDX + WebView2 + NAudio cannot compile on Linux without a language/UI rewrite (explicitly later).
revisit: After RTs and input land, fold scenes into Client.Linux rather than ifdeffing every form.

decision: RGBA PNG + BC3 sidecar, not a content-cut pack
why: GPU-friendly compression exists as a lever; PNG remains the readable fallback.
revisit: Swap range-fit BC3 for a higher-quality encoder if banding shows on UI.

decision: No C++/Rust rewrite this phase
why: Goal text: language rewrite only after bake+render land.
revisit: Revisit after Linux login→equip gate.

decision: Streaming atlas packer (per-image blit, flush full sheets, drop BGRA)
why: A real client Data tree is ~7GB+; holding every decoded library is fatal. Coverage still lists every missing catalog slot.
revisit: If a single multi-GB .Lib still spikes RSS, parse that file with a tighter on-disk window.

decision: Software WTL DXT (v1 RLE+block, v2 zlib+DXT1/3/5) in Crystal.Assets
why: Editor path used GDI+ / ManagedSquish / Ionic; Linux bake cannot. Do not invent texels for unknown types.
revisit: Re-run ImageDecodePercent on an operator Data pack; remaining gaps are format variants, not stubs.

decision: CMain : Form + DXManager frame facade; screenshot stays in the SlimDX adapter
why: Removes RenderForm / Device.GetBackBuffer from scene code so Linux is not coupled to SlimDX types.
revisit: Replace the WinForms message loop when scenes move into Client.Linux.

decision: Particles use System.Numerics.Vector2
why: SlimDX.Vector2 was the last game-logic vector type on the draw path.
revisit: None unless a leftover SlimDX math type appears.

decision: Client.Linux uploads bake atlas PNGs and DrawQuads catalog sprites
why: Proves the OpenGL/Null backends consume a real catalog, not a throwaway solid quad. Headless stays for CI; --frames exits windowed.
revisit: Swap PNG upload for BC3/S3TC when Linux drivers expose it.

decision: Server.Linux console host; Server.MirForms stays WinExe
why: Server.Library is already net8.0. WinForms + CustomFormControl cannot compile on Linux. Same Envir listen path.
revisit: Fold admin UI later or keep it Windows-only.

decision: ListenWithoutWorld + --root for external Jev DB
why: A missing Maps/MirDB must not block proving port 7000. Do not vendor Crystal.Database.
revisit: Turn the flag off when a complete Jev tree is on the box.

decision: Client.Linux --connect uses Shared Packet framing
why: Same Connected/ClientVersion/Login as Client.MirNetwork. No protocol rewrite.
revisit: Replace the stub host with LoginScene once scenes fold into Client.Linux.

decision: Full Jev --root starts Envir without --listen-without-world
why: Maps + Server.MirDB are enough to leave handshake-only mode. Flag is ignored when those files exist so StartGame cannot be silently disabled.
revisit: Keep --listen-without-world for empty CI roots only.

decision: Client.Linux MapView reuses Crystal MapReader + catalog/.Lib via IRenderer
why: GameScene stays WinForms. Linux draws floor/objects from Shared MapInformation + existing texels (low-fi remap, no invented art).
revisit: Fold real GameScene when the Windows TFM is no longer required.

decision: Phase E uses Shared Attack/PickUp/EquipItem plus existing TestServer @ commands
why: No new protocol. --test-server only flips Settings.TestServer so @MOB/@MAKE work.
revisit: Replace scripted verbs with Silk.NET input when scenes fold in.

decision: Silk.NET input + IRenderer HUD; WinForms dialogs stay stubbed
why: Same C.Walk/C.Attack as Crystal. Headless --input-script proves the loop without DISPLAY. Audio/WebView2 deferred.
revisit: Fold more GameScene dialogs when they no longer need WinForms.

decision: Inventory/equip/belt/skill HUD from Shared UserItem + ClientMagic
why: No WIL icons. Belt is inventory slots 0-5 (BeltDialog). Skill bar is 8 stubs.
revisit: Replace stubs with MagIcon/Items libs when a real catalog sheet exists.

decision: Mini-map is geometry from MapReader size + MapCell occupancy; C.Chat via Chat: token
why: MMap.Lib / MiniMap index stay unused (no invented map art). Same Shared C.Chat as Crystal.
revisit: Swap geometry for real MMap tiles only when that catalog slot exists on disk.

decision: NPC talk uses C.CallNPC [@Main] + S.NPCResponse; Linux NPC paths normalize backslashes
why: Same packets as GameScene click. Goods/quest only if those packets arrive. Trade/drag-drop stay stubbed.
revisit: WinForms NPCDialog graph remains Windows-only.

decision: NPC Buy/Sell via C.BuyItem/C.SellItem from --input-script + existing NPCGoods UniqueIDs
why: Same packets as NPCDialogs. Gold/bag proven in logs + HUD. Player trade deferred (needs a second online character).
revisit: Fold WinForms NPC buy UI when GameScene lands.

decision: Player trade via two Client.Linux processes + Shared Trade* packets
why: One login per account, so linux + linux2. Must face each other (C.Turn / @MOVE). Same C.TradeRequest/Reply/Gold/Confirm as GameScene.
revisit: WinForms TradeDialog stays Windows-only.

decision: Inventory bag move via C.MoveItem/C.MergeItem from --input-script Drag:from,to
why: Same packets as MirItemCell. Packet-level + HUD slot refresh; mouse-drag chrome deferred. Move:x:y stays map @MOVE.
revisit: WIL item icons / SelectedCell ghost when a catalog sheet exists.

decision: IAudio + Silk.NET OpenAL on Linux; Windows SoundManager stays NAudio
why: Same split as IRenderer/SlimDX. Headless uses Null so PlayGate never opens a device. Fixture wav is not game art; operator Sound packs stay outside git.
revisit: Fold SoundManager onto IAudio when GameScene lands on Linux.
